title: SecretsPaneClosed
description: The secrets.paneClosed JSON-RPC notification: the renderer telling the backend that a pane closed, so that pane's PENDING CAPTURES die with it (nocx-tsajw). Renderer-initiated and one-way — it has no response, which is exactly where an addressing defect would hide, and why it gets the same three checks as a method. IT WAS CALLED pane.close AND WAS RENAMED (nocx-isoph.4): the layout chain gained a real removal method, panes.close, and two methods one letter apart, meaning 'a pane is gone' and 'remove the pane from the durable chain', is the two-surfaces-one-word defect AGENTS.md names — the loser goes on advertising what it can no longer deliver. So the destructive act on the durable object is panes.close, in the layout family, and THIS is an event notification to the domain that already owns a pending capture (secrets.captureSave, secrets.captureDismiss), named in the past tense because it reports something that happened rather than asking for something. The two are not merged and must not be: closing a pane's capture scope touches no store and needs no answer, while removing a pane rewrites three tables and can mint a replacement.

paneId.description: The identity of the pane that closed — the same pane id the layout chain stores and history.record carries, minted once per pane by the renderer as a UUIDv7 and never reused, so a pane has ONE identity and not one per seam. Opaque to this handler: it is a capture SCOPE key here, bound to the connection the notification arrives on so a pane id from one connection can never reach another's captures, and the layout's UUIDv7 shape rule is deliberately not restated on it — this domain stores no pane and has no id of its own to conflict with, and a second statement of one rule is a second thing to keep in step.
